summary: This Wikipedia article describes the Equator as the imaginary line at 0° latitude dividing Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres, about 40,075 km in circumference. It covers the term's etymology, the equator's geodesy (precise location, exact length, and measurement standards), the eleven sovereign states it passes through, and its stable equatorial seasons and climate. It also briefly notes maritime line-crossing ceremonies.
one_line: Wikipedia article on the Equator, the 0° latitude line dividing Earth into hemispheres, covering its geodesy, countries crossed, and climate.
key_facts: The Equator is an imaginary line located at 0 degrees latitude, about 40,075 km (24,901 mi) in circumference, halfway between the North and South poles.
The name derives from medieval Latin aequator, in the phrase circulus aequator diei et noctis, meaning 'circle equalizing day and night'.
The equator is the only line of latitude which is also a great circle.
Sites near the Equator, such as the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou, French Guiana, have the fastest rotational speed of any latitude, 460 m (1,509 ft)/sec.
The true equatorial plane drifts about 9 metres (30 ft) during a year because Earth's rotation axis drifts.
The IAU 2009 value for the equatorial radius is 6,378.1366 km (3,963.1903 mi).
The WGS 84 standard has an equatorial radius of 6,378.137 km (3,963.191 mi), giving an equator length of 40,075.0167 km (24,901.4609 mi).
The geographical mile is defined as one arc-minute of the Equator; by WGS-84 it is 1,855.3248 metres (6,087.024 ft).
Earth is commonly modeled as a sphere flattened 0.336% along its axis, making the Equator 0.16% longer than a meridian.
The Equator passes through the land of eleven sovereign states, and Indonesia straddles the greatest length of the equatorial line across land and sea.
Despite its name, no part of Equatorial Guinea lies on the Equator; its island of Annobón is 155 km (96 mi) south of the Equator.
Near the equator, maximum solar radiation is received during the equinoxes, and temperatures are high year-round.
Average annual temperatures in equatorial lowlands are around 31 °C (88 °F) in the afternoon and 23 °C (73 °F) around sunrise.
The highest point on the equator is 4,690 metres (15,387 ft), on the southern slopes of Volcán Cayambe in Ecuador, and is the only place on the equator where snow lies on the ground.
Milder line-crossing ceremonies, typically featuring King Neptune, are held for passengers' entertainment on some civilian ocean liners and cruise ships.
